newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Tatarstan adopts own oil and gas law - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Tatarstan adopts own oil and gas law - newspaper.

text.p: Russia's autonomous republic of Tatarstan has passed an oil and gas law and adopted a resolution on the list of desposits to be developed on production-sharing terms, Russia's business daily Kommersant said on Wednesday.

The paper said Tatarstan had also announced that as an autonomous government, it did not have to get approval from Russia's State Duma lower house of parliament for the right to develop its fields under production-sharing agreements.
The Duma is in the process of looking at a list of 25 or so mineral reserves in Russia which were open to development under production-sharing agreement terms.
But the list, and enabling legislation needed for production sharing-agreements to begin operating, has been blocked by opposition among conservatives and nationalists in the Duma.
Tatarstan's decision to act alone was probably prompted by its frustration at Moscow's failure to push the list and legislation through, a lawyer familiar with production-sharing agreements said.
But it was not yet clear whether the region will be able to act independently of Moscow in the sensitive area of oil and gas, lawyers and analysts said.

"It is not clear so far whether the federal Duma may or may not veto this law, because of unclear distribution of authority between Tatarstan and the Russian Federation," said Moscow-based brokers Centreinvest Securities in a commentary.
"I don't think it will be as simple as the Tatarstan authorities might think," the lawyer added.
Despite legislative uncertainty, the law and resolution were still seen as a positive step for the region's oil industry.
"The adoption of the production-sharing law with the specified list of oil deposits is another breakthough," CentreInvest said.
The law calls for economic benefits to oil companies, and Kommersant quoted experts as saying that oil output would increase sharply if production-sharing agreements were adopted.
One of the main beneficiaries of the law and resolution, should they be allowed to proceed, would be regional oil company AO Tatneft TATN.RTS, one of Russia's top five producers.

The company produced 23.70 million tonnes of oil (474,000 barrels per day) last year compared with 24.14 million (483,000 bpd) in 1995. It has said it plans to produce 22.1 million tonnes (442,000 bpd) in 1997.
"The strong possibility of its implementation and consequent economic benefits for Tatneft should increase its share value," CentreInvest said.
Tatneft shares on the Russian Trading System were last trading at $80.40 at 1435 GMT, up $3.40 or 4.4 percent from Tuesday's close.
